AGIBOT releases physical-reasoning data linking decisions to actions

Release 4 varies starting conditions around shared goals and includes success and error annotations; the repository carries a non-commercial license.

Humanoids Daily ↗23 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

One goal, different action sequences

Announced on October 22, Physical Reasoning is AGIBOT WORLD 2026 Release 4. Restocking a minibar with three full bottles requires identifying empty bottles, counting existing stock and deciding what to add or remove instead of replaying a fixed motion sequence.

Annotations connect intent and execution

The data links questions, answers, high-level instructions, subtasks and action trajectories. Labels describe objects, locations, arm roles, gripper states and expected outcomes. Nine reasoning categories and three difficulty levels include erroneous examples for studying mistake detection and recovery.

A research resource with conditions

AGIBOT says it is using the data for an upcoming agent framework and model, but reports neither a Release 4 episode count nor measured success-rate gains. The Hugging Face repository lists CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, including a non-commercial restriction; product developers need to check the terms.
